name: Terracotta Courtyard Villa
concept: A single-storey Mediterranean-Caribbean villa composed as a calm, low-slung sequence of cream stucco pavilions beneath warm terracotta pitched roofs. The plan places the open living, dining and kitchen heart directly toward the pool and veranda, while three generous bedrooms occupy quieter wings for privacy. Natural stone anchors the arrival and garden elevations; broad glazed openings dissolve the boundary between interior rooms, shaded terraces and tropical garden.
hierarchy: Arrival pavilion: a welcoming, covered entry volume with a stone-faced threshold and clear view through to the garden.
Central social pavilion: the largest mass, containing the open-plan living, dining and modern kitchen, with the principal roof ridge and broad pool-facing glazing.
Private bedroom wing: a quieter linear wing for the three bedrooms and two bathrooms, articulated with recessed entries and shaded windows.
Pool veranda pavilion: a deep covered outdoor room extending from the social pavilion, framing the rectangular pool and linking to open sun terraces.
Service/arrival edge: discreet driveway, parking approach and screened utility planting kept separate from the pool garden.
roofLanguage: Warm terracotta, low-to-medium pitched gable roofs give the villa its Mediterranean-Caribbean identity. The main social pavilion receives the dominant gable, with secondary parallel or perpendicular pitched roofs stepping down over the bedroom and arrival volumes. Deep eaves, simple timber-toned soffits and restrained stone chimney-like accents add shade, depth and a crafted resort character.
entrance: Approach from a landscaped driveway to a sheltered covered porch recessed beneath a terracotta roof. Cream stucco walls are thickened around the doorway, with natural stone cladding at the entry plinth and one feature wall. A generous timber entry door, side glazing and planted forecourt establish a warm, legible arrival without exposing private bedroom windows.
outdoorLiving: The living and dining area opens fully onto a generous covered veranda sized as an outdoor lounge and dining room. This veranda overlooks a rectangular swimming pool, with connected limestone-toned terraces for loungers and informal gathering. A shaded outdoor kitchen or barbecue niche may sit at one end of the veranda, while open terrace zones preserve sunlight around the pool.
landscape: Tropical planting creates a layered setting on the flat site: palms and specimen frangipani define arrival and pool views; clipped low hedges and flowering shrubs soften architectural edges; broad-leaf planting screens bedrooms and service areas. A formal lawn and simple stone paths connect the driveway, entrance, veranda and pool terraces. Keep the pool garden open and sunlit, with denser planting at boundaries for privacy.
